Question 1 [4 marks]: Explain how Greenacre represents the value of shared experiences.
STIMULUS / TEXTS PROVIDED:
Text 1 — Poem
          Time Capsule
Sitting on the kitchen shelf
the tea leaves tin
held pride of place
in the running of the house
from breakfast through to dinner.
‘Would you like a cup of tea?’
my mother would question
one and all as a welcome
and a kind of mental setting
for family and guests.
Many lives and times have
passed through that tin,
the ritual of ‘one for each
person and one for the pot’
almost counting out our years
as a family of four children
was suddenly one at home
and I can still see them all
waiting round the table
for the tea to brew
until my father would pour
each cup carefully,
not one drop would he spill.
Into the seventies
the teapot reigned supreme
until suddenly the tea bag
had slipped in like a sniper,
picking off the minutes
of conversation, as if
there was no time to lose.
Now we sift through our parents
belongings to share what can
be sold or used and I grab
the tea leaves tin, thinking this,
of all things drew our family
together, by cup, by spoon.
                  MIKE GREENACRE
               Courtesy of Mike Greenacre

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 4):
4 marks: Explains effectively how Greenacre represents the value of shared experiences using well-chosen supporting evidence
3 marks: Explains how Greenacre represents the value of shared experiences using some supporting evidence
2 marks: Describes how Greenacre represents the value of shared experiences using limited supporting evidence
1 marks: Provides some relevant information about the text

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
Greenacre represents the value of shared experiences through the ritual of making tea that keeps this family close. The symbolic ‘tea leaves tin’ is central to the family’s shared moments and ‘held pride of place/in the running of the house’. The speaker’s nostalgic tone highlights the value of shared time as a family, ‘and I can still see them all / waiting around the table’. Greenacre suggests that objects provide a tangible link to shared family experiences across time: ‘this, of all things drew our family together, by cup, by spoon’ reinforcing the lasting value of family connection.
